chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the free man marrying the slave woman, or a slave marrying a free woman. So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The child would not be enslaved when one of its parents was free. It would be attached with the free one of the two, whichever of them, be it a father or a mother'.

key_terms.يُسْتَرَقُّ: To be enslaved / become a slave

ai.seo_question: What is the status of a child born to one free parent and one slave parent in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of 'ilqab' (attachment) in mixed-status unions, ruling that the child inherits the free status of the free parent, thereby avoiding enslavement. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it ensures social mobility and clarifies lineage, distinguishing it from other schools that may prioritize the father's status. The hadith underscores the mercy and justice inherent in the Imams' legal interpretations regarding family structures in early Islamic society.
